Cause and effect sentences are statements that explain the reasons for something and the results of a situation. You use words like since, because, therefore or consequently to organize your sentences in a cause and effect paragraph.

Cause and effect paragraphs generally follow a typical paragraph format. They are introduced by a topic sentence stating the general idea of the paragraph. They are then followed by sentences giving specific supporting details.
For example, if the topic sentence introduces an effect, the supporting sentences will describe its causes.

Example:
Factory jobs attracted more people (cause), as a result, cities have grown very large (effect).
Better schools were built in the area (cause) , consequently, it attracted more families (effect).
You organize your cause and effect paragraph with words like since, because, consequently, as a result of, therefore, due to/because + noun.

Example:
Cities have grown very large as a result of an increased effort to make downtown safer and more affordable. Due to the concentration of factory jobs, more people have been coming back to the city center.
Read the following examples from the text:
Consequently, relationships can be destroyed through arguments and violent outbursts leading to spousal and child abuse.
As a result, people become more self-centered, develop low self-esteem, doing things or behaving in ways that they would not normally.
Therefore, they have little or no regard to the outcomes of what is said or done during these periods.
Due to memory problems, alcoholics may not recognize the pain they are causing their families.

You use reason clauses to express the reasons for an action, or why a situation is the way it is.
You use words like because of, due to, and owing to to introduce a noun phrase to give a reason for something.

Reason clauses are subordinate to the main clause. They state the reason why things are done, or what makes a situation the way it is.
You can use the following words to write reason clauses:

• because
You use because to explain the reason why something is the way it is.

• since/as
You use since or as to introduce a reason that is already known.

• because of / on account of
You use because of/on account of with a noun phrase to talk about the reason behind an action or a situation.

images.text: Alcoholism is a disease that is characterized by the sufferer having a pattern of drinking that affects their life. Drinking excessively can result in a number of negative consequences, including  the deterioration of one's health and the destruction of family connections and external relationships. First, drinking can have a significant impact on your body and can lead to severe illness.  Signs of intoxication include the smell of alcohol, glazed or bloodshot eyes, and the deterioration in the person's appearance or hygiene.

Some health consequences include kidney failure, liver disease and in some cases death. Since the disease affects a person's entire system, children can be born with major health complications or in some cases, be stillborn. Alcohol can also have a very serious affect on a person's temperament. Drinking has negative side effects on self-esteem and rational thinking. As a result, people become more self-centered, develop low self-esteem, doing things or behaving in ways that are uncommon for them. Therefore, they have little or no regard to the outcomes of what is said or done during these periods. Oftentimes, they are unaware of their impact on others because of the disease's effect on memory.

Sufferers are unable to maintain healthy relationships because they are unable to control their addiction. Consequently, relationships can be destroyed through arguments and violent outbursts leading to spousal and child abuse. Relationships outside the family can be destroyed because of foolish arguments, inappropriate behavior and unreliability. Overall, alcoholism affects all facets of a person's  life, and can seriously  jeopardize their health, relationships and future.  They require intervention and tailored programs in order to deal with their addiction and successfully reintegrate themselves back into their communities.
